speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me narrow down the cause, could you describe exactly what the sensation feels like and how long each episode lasts?

Also, do you notice any associated symptoms like hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or trouble walking?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. Since the dizziness is position-dependent and you have a history of hearing loss, I need to confirm if these episodes are triggered specifically by turning your head in bed or looking up. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV

speaker: Patient

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in an elderly patient with hearing loss is classic for BPPV. I recommend the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected semicircular canal.
